seed: The short form of the speed walk, exactly as a person running Next gets it with no flag touched: the 6 minute reference edit opens, plays a minute at 1x across its transitions (frames due against frames shown, the worst gap between two new pictures, the same per transition, and what the sound engine left out), the playhead is dragged end to end at a medium speed and then across ten seconds at five times its playing speed, the way a person hunts for a moment (how many display frames the picture trails the hand, and how many the frame under the hand does: the canvas answers a move at once with the nearest frame it has read, so the two differ), and edits are made while it plays (the longest main thread pass each causes, counted under the pick the window really has when it is made): nothing at all first, the floor every edit stands on, then a trim and an undo with nothing picked, a clip moved half a second, a dissolve put on a cut ahead and a title reworded (each while it plays on, the way Final Cut keeps playing through them), then a pick of the recording under the playhead (the click that builds the panel's ten sections from nothing), nothing again, a trim, an undo, a blade (B cuts the clip in hand) and its undo with that clip picked, the way a person editing a clip has it, then a pick of another clip, then the clip is let go and picked again from nothing, and last play stops and starts again so the panel holds every section of the clip, and it is picked off and let go that way. Then thirty seconds of it from 0:50, a cube and three dissolves, are exported at the sheet's defaults (MP4, Standard, Full), timed with the longest main thread pass while it writes, and the most memory the app used from its launch to the end of the walk is kept beside the rest. Every number goes into speed.json and the run fails on any number worse than the baseline in Scripts/perf/baselines/short-6.json by more than its margin (50 per cent: since the long edit stopped stalling on 2026-11-13 one run differs from the next by about a fifth; the baseline is the worst of three runs) plus a small floor, apart from the medium drag's exact-frame lags, which are written down but not judged (a hand crossing the edit in seconds lands on whichever read finished first: 17 to 81 refreshes at the median on unchanged code). The long form, on the 6, 20 and 60 minute edits, is Scripts/perf/speed-walk.sh --long and never runs in the walk set.
